oddOneOut.concept: they are all fruit
oddOneOut.why: A carrot is a vegetable — it is the root of the plant, not the part that carries its seeds.

oddOneOut.concept: each one is worn on your feet
oddOneOut.why: A glove is worn, but on a hand.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all sports balls
oddOneOut.why: A die is used in games too, but you roll it rather than throw or kick it, and it is not a ball.

oddOneOut.concept: they all have wheels
oddOneOut.why: A canoe carries people the way the others do, but it slides through water on nothing at all.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all musical instruments
oddOneOut.why: A microphone carries sound to a loudspeaker; it makes no sound of its own.

oddOneOut.concept: they all give off their own light
oddOneOut.why: A mirror looks bright, but it only sends back light that something else made.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all birds
oddOneOut.why: A bat flies and has wings, but it is a mammal — it has fur and feeds its young on milk.

oddOneOut.concept: each one is used for writing or drawing
oddOneOut.why: A ruler guides a line and measures it, but it leaves no mark of its own.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all tools for building
oddOneOut.why: A brick is what gets built with, not what does the building.

oddOneOut.concept: they all float
oddOneOut.why: An anchor is made to do the opposite: it sinks, and holds a boat in place.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all clothes
oddOneOut.why: A handbag is carried rather than worn, and nothing goes inside it but your things.

oddOneOut.concept: every one of them tells you the time
oddOneOut.why: A compass has a dial and a moving needle like a clock, but it tells you which way you are facing.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all insects
oddOneOut.why: A spider has eight legs and no wings; every insect has six legs and three body parts.

oddOneOut.concept: they all keep the rain off you
oddOneOut.why: Sunglasses are for bright weather, not wet weather — they keep light out, not water.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all buildings
oddOneOut.why: A bridge is built, but nobody lives or works inside it — it carries you across.

oddOneOut.concept: they all come from a plant
oddOneOut.why: An egg is laid by a bird; everything else here was grown.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all sea animals
oddOneOut.why: An eagle hunts fish and flies over the sea, but it lives in the air and on land.

oddOneOut.concept: each one measures something
oddOneOut.why: A magnifying glass makes things look bigger; it never tells you how big they are.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all kinds of weather
oddOneOut.why: A thermometer measures the weather; it is not weather itself.

oddOneOut.concept: each one has a shell
oddOneOut.why: A frog has bare, damp skin and nothing hard on the outside.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all mammals
oddOneOut.why: A dolphin lives in the sea but is still a mammal; a penguin is a bird, with feathers and eggs.

oddOneOut.concept: all of them fly with no engine
oddOneOut.why: A helicopter stays up only while its engine runs.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all trees or plants
oddOneOut.why: A mushroom is a fungus: it has no leaves and makes no food from sunlight.

oddOneOut.concept: they all need electricity to work
oddOneOut.why: A candle makes its light by burning, with no electricity at all.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all parts of your body
oddOneOut.why: A cap goes on a body, but it is not part of one.

oddOneOut.concept: each one is made of glass
oddOneOut.why: A brick is baked clay — hard like glass, but you cannot see through it.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all things you find in a kitchen
oddOneOut.why: A toothbrush belongs in a bathroom; everything else here is for cooking or eating.

oddOneOut.concept: every one of them holds water
oddOneOut.why: A basket is a container too, but water runs straight out through the weave.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all found in the sky
oddOneOut.why: A wave belongs to the sea, however high it rises.

oddOneOut.concept: each one is frozen
oddOneOut.why: Fire is the one thing here that melts the rest.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all ways of travelling on land
oddOneOut.why: A sailing boat carries you, but only across water.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all made of metal
oddOneOut.why: A log is wood — it floats, it burns, and it was once alive.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all written or printed to be read
oddOneOut.why: A crayon is what you write with, not something written.

oddOneOut.concept: each one of them can be eaten
oddOneOut.why: Soap is shaped and wrapped like food, and it is the one thing here you must not eat.

oddOneOut.concept: they are all reptiles
oddOneOut.why: A frog is an amphibian: it starts life in water as a tadpole and keeps damp skin.

oddOneOut.concept: every one of them gives out heat
oddOneOut.why: An ice cube does the opposite — it takes heat out of whatever it touches.
